finding.title: Fowler. Section 6 calls P1 "commands with no gate" but P1 includes four commands that have a gate row. `explain` (`--format interactive` refused, `spec:108`), `business-panel` (socratic refused, `spec:102`), `test` (`--watch` refused, `spec:123`), `index` (knowledge-base statement, `spec:111`). The gate-trigger acceptance check (AC-2.2, `spec:200`) is defined for P2 commands only, so P1 never tests those refusals.

e1.context:
| Phase | Scope | Commands | Why this order |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P0. Contract and live baseline** (no command edits) | Write `src/superclaude/core/WORKER-CONTRACT.md` (section 2 rules plus a coordinator brief template listing the section 3.1 flags), add it to `KNOWN_CORE_FILES`, add an Orca section to `HOW-WE-WORK.md` and its two mirrored copies, and add the static test file `tests/skills/test_worker_contract.py` (proposed name). Then run three ready commands as real Orca workers, invoked directly, to close evidence gap 1.4 (1). | Smoke runs: `/sc:troubleshoot` (no `--fix`), `/sc:workflow --handoff none`, `/sc:adversarial --output <dir>` | Uses only the 10 ready commands, so the coordinator gets value before any command changes, and the smoke runs test the decision before anything is built on it. |
| **P1. Report files and commands with no gate** | The WC-4 contract in unattended mode; the `--unattended` flag accepted by every command in sections 3.1 and 3.2 (a no-op where a command has no gate); output flags for commands that lack one; the small fixes to ready commands. | analyze, build, business-panel, design, document, explain, index, test, load (usage line only); fixes to adversarial, cleanup-audit, index-repo, workflow | No person gate is involved, so each change is mechanical and gives every later phase a report file to check. |
| **P2. Gate conversion** | Each default-on gate resolves per its section 3 row; WC-10 wait splitting for cli-eval. | auggie-review, cleanup, improve, cli-eval, cli-portify, recommend, research, review-translation, spec-panel, task, tasklist, reflect, release-split, tdd, troubleshoot | The main blocker class (`INV-A:96`, `INV-B:292`). These changes touch no safety rule and add no outward capability; where a command has an outward default (auggie-review posting, task's `commit`/`push` and committed TFEP report), P2 only turns it off under `--unattended` (WC-9). |
| **P3. Interface drift and shared state** | Reconcile command and skill where they disagree; make memory writes parallel-safe. | roadmap, validate-roadmap, validate-tests, save | These are defects today regardless of Orca (`INV-B:294,296`); the coordinator cannot predict their report path until they are fixed. |
| **P4. Outward actions and safety rules** | Apply the answers to D2-D4: the implement halt path, post-release pre-authorization, pr-submit as a worker. | implement, post-release, pr-submit | Each one either changes a deliberate safety rule (`sk/sc-implement-protocol/refs/qa.md:238`) or performs outward actions (`sk/sc-pr-submit-protocol/SKILL.md:189,196`; `sk/sc-post-release-protocol/SKILL.md:340,351`), so it needs the user's decision first. |
